text:
maria: Quick note — planning a non-urgent deploy tonight 18:00 UTC for inference-orch v1.8 (routing + small observability work). I want to align on smoke checks and the minimal dashboard/alert tweaks we'll push along with it.

alex: Who's actually doing the deploy? I can be on-call for the window if needed.

maria: @alex, thanks — you're the owner for the rollout. I'll stay on watch for dashboards. Taylor will validate traces/latency.

alex: ok, I'll kick it off at :hourglass: 18:00 UTC. Plan: canary -> 10% for 10m -> 50% -> 100% if no regressions. Will post timestamps.

taylor: Observability changes:
- Dashboard: add a small panel to show per-model p95 latency (seq_len=512) across regions.
- Traces: add a tag `deploy_id` on root span so we can filter canary requests.
- Alerts: temporarily raise the p95 latency alert threshold from 400ms -> 650ms during canary to avoid noisy pages; will revert after rollout.

sahil: Quick question — do we need to change token-cost billing metrics? This deploy doesn't affect batching but does swap a routing policy.

maria: @sahil no billing metric changes. Just routing optimization (prefer cheaper model variant when capacity low). No cost-metric touch.

jamie: Code review ping: PR #4682 (orch routing config) needs one more approval from infra. @alex can you merge after smoke?

alex: will wait to merge until after the canary passes. I want to be able to rollback quickly if metrics spike.

taylor: Smoke checklist (what I'll verify):
1) p95 latency panel shows <= 600ms for canary group
2) error rate (5xx) < 0.5% on canary
3) traces: `deploy_id` present and trace sampling looks normal
4) tail latency histogram for seq_len 1/128/512 looks sane

maria: I'll apply dashboard changes as a patch to the infra-dashboards repo before the window. patch: `git commit -m "add p95 panel + deploy_id filter"`

alex: rollback plan:
- immediate: cut canary -> 0% routing (route all traffic to previous model)
- follow-up: apply previous config (tagged v1.7) from s3: s3://redwood-configs/orch/v1.7.json and restart router pods gracefully
- paging: if error rate > 2% for 5m or p95 > 1s for 3m, escalate to oncall and consider rollback

sahil: For alerts, who will temporarily bump thresholds? Is that automated or manual?

taylor: I'll push a short-lived patch to the alerting rules: `increase p95_alert_threshold for orch-routing from 400 to 650` and annotate with `# deploy 1912345000` so we can find it to revert.

maria: tagging owners for visibility: @jamie (dash review), @sahil (cost/metrics), @taylor (alert changes).

jamie: Quick review comment — can we make the p95 panel split by `model_variant`? helps see fallback behavior.

taylor: good call, will add `model_variant` breakdown, keep y-axis shared.

deploy-bot: [deploy scheduled] inference-orch v1.8 by alex at 1912346400 (18:00:00 UTC). Canary steps: 10% (10m) -> 50% (10m) -> 100%.

alex: starting canary now (18:00 UTC). pushing rollout id=ro-1912345000-canary

taylor: saw `deploy_id` in traces, can confirm the tag, sampling looks as expected. p95 currently 420ms on canary.

maria: dashboard patch merged and applied, note added in infra-dashboards changelog.

alex: shifting to 50% -> 18:10 UTC

taylor: p95 stable 430-470ms, error rate 0.12% on canary. Histograms look ok.

sahil: cost signals stable, no unexpected spikes in tokens/sec.

alex: moving to 100% at 18:20 UTC

deploy-bot: [deploy complete] inference-orch v1.8 rolled to 100% at 1912346200.

taylor: post-rollout checks passing. I'll revert the alert threshold bump in 30m and remove the deploy-specific annotation.

maria: thanks everyone. tagging this thread for the release notes: obs changes, alert threshold bump during canary, deploy_id tracing tag, dash panel addition.

alex: closing loop — PR #4682 merged to main and tagged v1.8. If anyone sees anything odd, ping here or page oncall. :thumbsup:
